newsitem.title: USA: More US high-grade corp bond supply expected soon. [CORRECTED 23:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: More US high-grade corp bond supply expected soon. [CORRECTED 23:00 GMT]

text.p: The forward calendar for new investment-grade corporate debt is building as issuers seek to capitalize on currently strong U.S. and global debt markets, syndicate officials said.
Rumors have surfaced that Merrill Lynch & Co is preparing a $1 billion global debt offering for Bayerische Landesbank early next week. Merrill officials would not comment.

Market attention is currently focused on two large global debt offerings that were recently launched: a $1 billion 10-year offering from Ford Motor Credit Corp and a $1 billion offering of 10-year bonds from the Asian Development Bank.
Price talk on the Ford deal, rated A1/A-plus, was set on Tuesday morning at a spread of 60 basis points over comparable Treasuries via Merrill Lynch (corrects to show deal has not yet been priced).
The ADB offering, rated AAA/AAA, priced at a spread of 18 basis points over comparable Treasuries via lead-managers Goldman Sachs & Co, SBC Warburg and Bank of Tokyo Mitsubishi.
Syndicate officials said both deals were priced aggressively which was a reflection of strong investor demand.
Market sources noted the ADB deal, which included 10 co-managers in its syndicate group, benefitted from a particularly strong marketing effort.
A collection of other investment-grade debt issuers were also readying deals for Tuesday.
Citicorp plans to sell $250 million in 10-year notes, rated A2/A, via Lehman Brothers Inc on Tuesday, market sources said. Price talk on the deal is around 58 basis points over Treasuries.
Branch Banking and Trust is also expected to sell $250 million in 10-year subordinated debt. Price talk for the A3/BBB-plus offering, is around 70 basis points over Treasuries, sources said.
Bear Stearns & Co Inc is the lead manager of the deal.
